clue.text: Heaps of dogs?

definitions.meaning: piles of stones raised as markers on hills
small Scottish terriers bred for working among stone piles; plural like the answer

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the word: mounds of stacked stones, and a breed of short-legged Highland terrier.

clue.text: Legislation that went against the grain

definitions.text: Legislation that went against the grain

parts.words: Legislation that went against the grain
parts.note: laws on cereal imports, which many felt worked against fair bread prices, read literally as rules opposing grain

explanation.definitionFit: Nineteenth-century British statutes taxing imported cereals, hated by the poor and repealed in 1846.

clue.text: Club regulation that must be strictly obeyed

definitions.text: Club regulation that must be strictly obeyed

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
a rule is a regulation

explanation.surface: A golf club's rulebook insists members follow every regulation without exception.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for harsh, unbending authority that permits no disobedience.

clue.text: Leon turned up for Christmas

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the name Leon is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A man called Leon arrived for the Christmas festivities.
explanation.definitionFit: A word for the festive season, familiar from carols.

clue.text: See lambs rounded up and put together

indicators.note: like sheep herded into a pen, the letters of see lambs are gathered into a new order

explanation.surface: A shepherd is told to watch the young sheep gathered into a flock.
explanation.definitionFit: To construct from parts, or to gather into one place.

clue.text: Old black marketeers?

parts.note: looks like illegal dealers of the past, but describes those who historically sold enslaved Africans

explanation.definitionFit: Merchants in the Atlantic trade in enslaved people, abolished in the British Empire in 1807.

clue.text: A marginal advantage

parts.note: a slight lead over a rival, and also something lying at the margin or border

explanation.definitionFit: A small superiority, as in having the upper hand, and also a rim or border.

clue.text: He gets the game off to a flying start

definitions.text: He gets the game off to a flying start

parts.words: He gets the game off to a flying start
parts.note: game here means birds shot for sport, driven into the air by someone thrashing the undergrowth

explanation.definitionFit: On a shoot, a person employed to flush pheasants or grouse from cover towards the guns.

clue.text: Get out of breath, being no longer fit

parts.note: ex describes a former partner or thing no longer current
hale means healthy and fit, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: Someone out of shape finds themselves panting after exertion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get out of breath' looks like panting; read it as pushing air out of the lungs.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe out, expelling air from the lungs.

clue.text: Created an uproar and disturbed the editor

indicators.note: the word editor is upset, its letters thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A protester made a scene and unsettled the newspaper's chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Ran wild in a violent public disturbance.

clue.text: Diagram representing quantities-of local sales?

parts.note: a chart with rectangles of varying length, whimsically read as a plot of a pub's takings

explanation.definitionFit: A chart using columns of different heights to compare amounts; the bar in the pub is the local.

clue.text: One by one?

parts.note: not a sequence but a picture painted by a person of that same person

explanation.definitionFit: An artist's depiction of themselves, a work by an individual of that individual.

clue.text: Learning to look about

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
re means about or concerning

explanation.definitionFit: Traditional knowledge handed down, a body of learning.

clue.text: Cut and serve out

indicators.note: out signals the word serve is put out of order

explanation.surface: A waiter slices and hands round portions.
explanation.definitionFit: To slice through or divide, synonymous with cut.

clue.text: Went over the hill

definitions.meaning: a mountain or moor in northern England

explanation.surface: A walker crossed the high ground.
explanation.walkthrough: A FELL is an upland hill in the Lake District and Pennines of northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of tumble down, and a northern English upland moor.

clue.text: Evict wild and smelly cat

indicators.note: wild signals the letters of evict running free in a new order

explanation.surface: Throw out a feral, stinking moggy.
explanation.definitionFit: A catlike African and Asian mammal noted for its musky scent glands.

clue.text: Sole member of the citrus family

definitions.text: Sole member of the citrus family

parts.words: Sole member of the citrus family
parts.note: sole looks like only, but it hints at a flatfish whose name pairs it with a sour yellow fruit

explanation.definitionFit: A sour yellow citrus fruit, which also names a flatfish, the lemon sole.

clue.text: Being knowledgeable remind fellow in difficulty

indicators.note: the words remind fellow are in trouble, their letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A clever person reminds a struggling colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a lot of knowledge, being well briefed.

clue.text: A girl outwardly competent and very charming

indicators.note: the girl's name has competent on the outside, wrapped around it

parts.note: able means competent
Dora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman appears capable and delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' means competent goes round the girl, splitting its synonym after the first letter; the opening 'A' is only a link word, not a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiring delight or affection; utterly lovely.

clue.text: Struggles to maintain faith in the past

definitions.text: Struggles to maintain faith in the past

parts.words: Struggles to maintain faith in the past
parts.note: fights for a belief, and historically medieval wars waged for the Christian religion

explanation.definitionFit: Medieval military expeditions to the Holy Land, and by extension vigorous campaigns for a cause.

clue.text: He has the best time of anyone

definitions.text: He has the best time of anyone

parts.words: He has the best time of anyone
parts.note: sounds like someone enjoying life most, but means an athlete holding the fastest time ever

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds the top performance mark, such as the fastest time in a race.

clue.text: Whinnies and bleats may come from it

definitions.text: Whinnies and bleats may come from it

parts.words: Whinnies and bleats may come from it
parts.note: animal noises heard from a building where horses and other livestock are housed

explanation.definitionFit: A building for housing horses, from which neighing would be heard.

clue.text: How the sailor and parson may join together

definitions.text: How the sailor and parson may join together

parts.words: How the sailor and parson may join together
parts.note: a seaman joins rope ends by interweaving strands, and a clergyman joins a couple in marriage

explanation.definitionFit: To interweave rope ends, and informally to marry, as in getting hitched.

clue.text: Make a recording of a band

explanation.definitionFit: To record on magnetic ribbon, and a narrow strip such as sticky ribbon or a finishing line.

clue.text: Tears out for a look

indicators.note: out signals the word tears is put out of order

explanation.surface: A tearful person rips something out to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: A long fixed gaze.

clue.text: Rainbow seen when in the garden

definitions.meaning: the Greek goddess personifying the rainbow
a flowering plant grown in garden beds

explanation.definitionFit: The rainbow goddess of Greek myth, and a garden flower with sword-shaped leaves.

clue.text: Island keys in storm

indicators.note: the word keys is tossed about as if at sea, its letters shuffled

explanation.surface: Low islands are battered by a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: SKYE is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A large Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides.

clue.text: Farm butter

parts.note: not a dairy product but a farmyard animal that butts with its horns

explanation.definitionFit: A horned farm animal that charges with its head.

clue.text: Criticism for a decent chap on strike

parts.note: a brick is old slang for a reliable good fellow
to bat is to hit or strike

explanation.surface: A good fellow on a picket line attracts disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh remark, originally a piece of masonry thrown in anger.

clue.text: Veto for proposal

parts.note: a bid is an offer or proposal

explanation.definitionFit: To prohibit or refuse to allow.

clue.text: The latest possible hour

parts.note: the last moment before it is too late, from the parable of labourers hired near day's end

explanation.definitionFit: An ordinal from the idiom for the last possible moment before a deadline.

clue.text: Beat nervous tension

definitions.meaning: emphasis in rhythm or on a syllable

explanation.definitionFit: Accent or emphasis in music or speech, and psychological strain.
